items.title: the rings of saturn
items.summaryPlot: in august 1992, a nameless german-born narrator (resembling sebald) sets off on a walking tour of the suffolk coast in england. what follows is not a straightforward travelogue but a hypnotic, digressive meditation: each step triggers layered reflections on history, literature, natural science, and decay—from sir thomas browne's skull and rembrandt's anatomy lesson to the herring's natural history, the congo atrocities of joseph conrad and roger casement, the firebombing of wwii, and the dowager empress tz'u-hsi's silkworms. exactly one year later, the narrator is admitted to a norwich hospital in a state of near-total immobility.
pros: transitions from physical paths in suffolk into sweeping historical, philosophical and biographical inquiries without jagged structural breaks.
examines the universal law of decay, demonstrating how empires, grand estates, ecosystems and human bodies inevitably collapse into dust. studies the inevitable.
features grainy black-and-white photographs, newspaper clippings and diagrams placed directly in the text without captions, it's haunting blend of documentary evidence and feels dreamy.
details the horrific exploitation of the belgian congo through the intersecting biographies of joseph conrad and roger casement with cold precision.
opens with 17th-century polymath sir thomas browne, using his dissection of quincunxes, skulls and urn burials to establish the book's metaphysics.
tells the landscapes of dunwich which is a medieval city lost to the sea and the abandoned cold war military installations at orford ness with earned atmospheric weight.
concludes with an historical analysis of sericulture (silk production), from imperial china to prussian state control and nazi metaphors.
refuses to romanticize the past.
telles the shadow of the holocaust through indirect reflections on ruined european spaces rather than generic explicit exposition.
it never forces any underdeveloped tension, unearned romance or a traditional plot when informing, never tries to be something it isn't unlike nineteen eighty four.
cons: text contains no chapter breaks, dialogue indents or traditional paragraph scaffolding, wall of text creates fatigue.
relies on deep familiarity with external factors such as european history, literature (chateaubriand, conrad, swinburne) and art history.
intentionally blends documented historical facts with fabricated biographical details, this is epistemological...
repeatedly details overgrown gardens, damp hotel rooms and foggy coastlines gets annoying.
mediumInfluences: the anatomy lesson of dr. nicolaes tulp

items.title: killer7
philosophicalTags: the dialectic of friend and enemy
items.summaryPlot: the game takes place in an alternate history where a fragile world peace is threatened by "heaven smiles," invisible, laughing, suicide-bomber mutants. you control harman smith, a wheelchair-bound assassin who can manifest seven distinct personalities—each with unique weapons and skills—collectively known as the killer7. hired by the u.s. government, the killer7 are sent to eliminate the heaven smiles and their creator, kun lan. as they carry out hits across the globe, they uncover a deep conspiracy involving the role of japan in u.s. politics and the true, shocking nature of their own existence.
pros: restricting movement to a run button along pre-determined track nodes turns environment into an rhythm-based puzzle.
first-person scanning and shooting mechanics force you to detonate yellow glowing weak points on camouflaged "heaven smiles" under time pressure.

switching between the 7 assassin personas with each with bespoke firearm caliber, reload speed, spatial abilitoes (kaede’s blood barrier piercing, con’s blind navigation, kevin’s invisibility) is boosts problem-solving and variety.
harvesting thick and thin blood from fallen smiles to upgrade attributes (power, speed, waver, critical) or recovery vials creates a tight resource management.
uses cold war remnants, nuclear disarmament treaties and shadow bureaucracy diplimacy between the us and japan for a geopolitical thriller.
comic book brutalism looking sharp geometric artwork.
memorable boss actions such as the power rangers parody "handsome men", curtis blackburn’s quick-draw duel and the wind-up ayame blackburn fight are over standard shooter tropes.
spoiler/ deconstruction of harman smith, kun lan and garcian smith’s true identities recontextualizes the gameplay into a psychological point..
cons: you cannot move when shooting.
monotonous branching node turning.
repetitive basic enemy encounters.
opening locks requires searching for soul rings and specific heads (iwazaru, travis) which feels lazy and annoying.
awkward hitbox misalignments.
once dan smith’s collateral shot and con smith’s agility are maxed out, certain personas like coyote or mask see less tactical utility..
puzzles are mostly seeks lazy trial-and-error where you try more than thinking.
lack of mid-mission fast travel.
political exposition told through disembodied ghosts seeks external reading to understand plot points which is huge deal for me.
similarMedia: metal gear solid 2 sons of liberty
el shaddai ascension of the metatron

items.title: phoenix
items.summaryPlot: a cosmic, immortal firebird known as the phoenix serves as a guide through a vast, non-linear anthology of stories spanning from the mythic past to the distant future. each self-contained part is set in a different era and explores humanity's endless, often destructive quest for immortality, power, and meaning, as the series delves into the cycle of life, death, and reincarnation that connects all living things.
pros: alternating chronologically from the ancient dawn of civilization and the far future extinction of mankind toward the present.
future arc depicts the heat death of earth and masato yamanobe’s billions of years in isolation as an immortal consciousness.
rejects romanticized immortality.
karma arc explores the rivalry between mutilated bandit gao and privileged sculptor akanemaru, painful reality of artistic creation versus sponsored corruption.
tracking the karmic lineage of the large-nosed saruta archetype through multiple distinct eras is a through-line of generational suffering and redemption in reincarnation mechanic.
avant-garde geometry is disintegrating.
masterfully serves 7th-century shinto-buddhist religious warfare with a 21st-century dystopian shadow society through linked spiritual dreaming.
manga refuses to sanitize ancient history, it depicts war, religious fanaticism, slavery and political purges with grounded approach.
spoiler/ setting dying astronauts to escape pods while managing hallucination alien parasites is tezuka's mastery of suspense and resource management.
cons: tezuka puts slapstick, 4th wall breaker modern celebrity cameos and meta-jokes that damages dark tension.
because of tezuka’s death in 1989, the manga is never finished. death is just another external factor so unfinished story is critically problematic to me ignoring the context.
dated disney-influenced character designs.
some volumes feel lightweight compared to pillars like "karma" or "future".
characters reach the phoenix only to realize too late the futility of human greed, which feels formulaic across multiple volumes.
underdeveloped side characters in shorter arcs.
similarMedia: nausicaä of the valley of the wind

items.title: a winged victory for the sullen
items.mainCreator: a winged victory for the sullen

creatorDetails.name: a winged victory for the sullen

items.summaryPlot: evokes the emotional and spiritual weight of loss, memory, and transcendence. it is a meditation on grief, particularly inspired by the death of mark linkous, blending ambient drone, neoclassical strings, and melancholic piano to create a vast, reflective, and deeply atmospheric soundscape.
pros: recorded in acoustically rich spaces (including berlin's grunewald church), with natural room decay, pedal creaks and bow scrapes with lifelike clarity.
seamlessly blends dustin o'halloran’s piano motifs with adam wiltzie’s (stars of the lid) layered ambient drones.
album is opened with with patient piano chords that slowly dissolve into aching cello lines.
features lush performances by peter broderick-led string ensemble, avoiding orchestral bombast for more harmonic play.
"steep hills of vicodin tears" is emotionally earned with warm analog drones beneath string chords.
phill brown and francesco donadello's mixing allows individual piano notes to decay naturally without frequency clutters.
bypasses cheap cinematic melodrama in for minimalism and meditation.
cons: harmonic pacing causes listening fatigue in the mid-sequences.
absence of percussive momentum or syncopated tension leaves the load on sustain pedals and sustained bow strokes so album overally becomes so rhythmless.
pieces like "minuet for a cheap piano number one" and "number two" share nearly identical formulas and dynamic.
relies a lot at ambeint formlessness that risks within the genre is barely taken. album is also considered as a drone album and it lacks the elemental catalog of the expected.
several tracks serve to a formula with sparse piano intro, string drone then decay to silence.
back half of the record slows its textural progression, reusing motifs used earlier on the tracklist.
similarMedia: stars of the lid and their refinement of the decline
an accidental memory in the case of death

items.title: night on the galactic railroad
items.summaryPlot: a poor and lonely boy named giovanni falls asleep on a hill during the star festival and dreams he is riding a magnificent train through the milky way with his beloved friend campanella. as they journey past celestial wonders, they encounter passengers who reveal themselves to be dead, and giovanni ultimately realizes his friend campanella has drowned in a river saving another boy, forcing him to confront the profound meaning of true happiness, self-sacrifice, and death.
pros: story begins with giovanni’s exhausting real-world labor, typesetting letters in a dark print shop and enduring poverty and bullying, which enforces the emotional weight.
train route charts milky way constellations and nebulae (northern cross, cygnus, scorpius, southern cross, coal sack), turning metaphysics into a transit.
thematic depth on true happiness with complex moral elements.
spoiler/ scorpion that laments its useless death and burns its own body to illuminate the darkness is effective thematic stone for selfless sacrifice.
spoiler/ campanella’s earned melancholy, wet coat and realization of his destination tell his physical death by drowning without melodrama.
encounter with the tutor and children from the sunken ocean liner tell the celestial train as a universal vessel for souls passing through tragedy.
digging up 1.2-million-year-old fossilized walnuts along the glowing river bed is a stunning section between paleontology and spiritual eternity.
rejection of easy religious dogmas with blending budhist concrpts of selflessness with christian iconography  such as hymns and southern cross into a metaphysical frame.
void of campanella's must into the infinite unknown, leaving giovanni alone.
spoiler/ giovanni wakes up under the stars to discover campanella’s death in the river, choosing to return home with milk for his mother and bear the burden of living.
cons: structure is shaky, i think because author revised until he died. external reason aside, you feel the fragmented execution.
giovanni is more of observant passenger in celestial sights rather than someome active in the conflict.
characters deliver direct metaphysical lectures on altruism that border on didactic sermonizing.
episodic structure of passengers sharing their grief at their respective afterlife stations feels formulaic
schoolyard bullies like zanelli are shallow characters designed specifically to serve single obvious personality and cause.
transition from grounded poverty to celestial surrealism is too sudden.
over-reliance on descriptions of glowing crystals, phosphorus sands and silver reeds causes fatigue during the middle parts.

items.title: depression cherry
items.summaryPlot: exploration of grief, loss, and the passage of time. it serves as a sonic and emotional landscape, using stripped-down, minimalist dream pop arrangements to evoke a specific feeling—described by the band as "a color, a place, a feeling, an energy". the album is a meditative journey through melancholy, designed to immerse the listener in a mood of bittersweet reflection and existential contemplation.
pros: "space song" is anchored by an iconic slide-guitar lead and a pulsating keyboard arpeggio.
minimalism works out with intentionally aggressive live drumming in favor of gentle drum machines and spacious organs with bedroom sounds.
"levitation" uses organ drone that layers victoria legrand’s vocal harmonies to open the record with depth.
layered vocal loops and distorted guitar fuzz serve textured burst of energy with shoegaze elements.
generous acoustic headroom around the vocals and hypnotic vocal layering.
"ppp" build on a 6/8 arpeggio that slowly comes up with harmonic tension before turning into a cinematic outro.
aesthetic of melancholic nostalgia, intimacy and slow-burn reverie.
very solid pacing with spaces for individual synth chords.
cons: formulaic song structures.
electronic drums are buried shallowly under everything else.
tracks like "bluebird" and "wildflower" feel lightweight and riskless.
impressionistic muffled lyricism that seeks external factors.
limited dynamic contrast.
reliance on yamaha ps-20 organ feels repetitive.
absence of dynamic basslines or shifting syncopation makes the harmonic rhythm kinda floaty.
similarMedia: ceres & calypso in the deep time

items.title: the princess and the pilot
items.summaryPlot: set in a world at war between the levamme empire and the amatsukami imperium, the mercenary pilot charles karino is given a mission: to fly the princess juana del moral alone across 12,000 kilometers of enemy territory so she can marry her fiancé, prince carlo, who has promised to end the war. during their journey, the two develop a bond that transcends their social divide, all while being hunted by the imperium's forces.
pros: combat serve genuine flight principles such as energy management, altitude advantage, stall speeds and cloud-cover breaking rather than hilarious aura farm.
story avoids a fairytale romance by acknowledging the inescapable political and class realities of their world, emotional separation and romance are earned.
class discrimination serve tension and thematic weight
aircraft is well designed; twin cockpits, realistic instrumentation and mechanical constraints like fuel weight and overheating engines.
main objective serve vulnerablity and tension.
madhouse’s open-ocean horizons, cumulonimbus clouds and sunset reflections enhances the sense of geographic feeling.
dogfight against the rival ace pilot has mutual tactics such as blind spots and sun positioning to outmart the enemy.
character interactions lacks unnecessary melodrama.
cons: sheltered royal who learns humility who discovers purpose follow well-trodden anime tropes.
flight pacing is damaged by repetitive dialogues, repetitive cockpit shots and still flying far from tension.
macro wars are background noise.
enemy acts dumb and blind on purpose to plot armor.
supporting characters on both military sides are flat.
ending focuses on the personal farewell. systemic societal oppression charles faces stays unresolved.

items.title: p.n.03
items.summaryPlot: in a futuristic space colony, a rogue computerized armament management system (cams) has turned its robot army against humanity. players control vanessa z. schneider, a freelance mercenary hired by a mysterious client to destroy the cams facilities and robots. as she fights through eleven linear levels, she uncovers secrets about the client's true motives and even discovers a clone of herself, which she is forced to abandon.
pros: dodging attacks consist of dance routine, utilizing cartwheels, ducking, backflips and side-steps with invulnerability frames.
aegis suit customization is clear progression.
laser grids, projectile paths and missile trajectories making the game skill-dependent.
chaining combos with countdown timer rewards awareness.
character movement is keyframed with slick and rhythmic visual identity.
arenas force you to quickly identify and eliminate turrets and long-range snipers first which is tactical prioritization.
user interface is sleek and clean.
cons: in an arcade shooting game, it's impossible to shoot when moving.
every single mission takes place in visually identical, grey-and-white hallways and industrial rooms.
progressing in harder difficulties requires replaying randomly generated "trial missions" to grind points for suit upgrades.
level design are opening a door, locking into a box room, clearing turrets and moving to the next identical room.
primary combat is about smashing the auto-targeting triggers zero combo variations and manual aiming is sluggish and imprecise.
repetitive robotic enemy types.
defensive roll often ends in dropped inputs due to animation recovery time, disappointing in sleek animations.
story is functionally barebones and delivered through minimal text, got zero emotional weight.

items.title: kya lost linage
items.summaryPlot: a young woman named kya and her brother frank are accidentally transported to a strange, magical world through a portal. after being separated, kya discovers that the world is terrorized by the evil brazul, who has been mutating the peaceful, cat-like nativs into savage werewolf-like creatures called the wolfen. kya learns that her own father, brazul, is responsible and has taken frank captive for his sinister experiments. kya must master her combat skills and explore floating islands to rescue her brother, defeat her corrupted father, and free the nativs.
pros: magical boomerang is both a kinetic weapon and a physics-based puzzle tool.
rescued nativs populate the hub village and open shops which feels progressive.
airstream boarding sequences require reading and reflexes to navigate.
boomerang upgrades like capturing different elemental types unlocks environmental progress.
ability to grapple, judo-throw and manipulate enemy hitboxes adds a layer of control to the melee.
floating level design feels layered and cohesive.
game relies on visual cues than ui elements.
cons: sluggish delayed melee input response.
stealth sections are lazy and inconsistent with all of the artificial gimmicks.
platforming feels very floaty and performative.
poor lock-on targeting is too unreliable that it causes frustration. combined with awkward camera angles, the game becomes pain in the ass sometimes.
wind-riding sections routinely place obstacles off-screen,  so you do fail and memorization rather than skill.
combat is about fighting the same wolfen variants with slightly increased health pools, lacks variety or any complex ai.
lack of fast travel causes annoying runbacks.
once specific combat upgrades like the multi-target guine are purchased, the combat loses all tactical value.
similarMedia: sly cooper and the thievius raccoonus
tak and the power of juju

items.title: camp lazlo
items.summaryPlot: set in a universe of anthropomorphic animals, the series follows lazlo, an eccentric and optimistic spider monkey, and his two best friends—raj, a timid indian elephant, and clam, a quiet albino pygmy rhinoceros—as they attend the poorly-run camp kidney. the trio's surreal misadventures often put them at odds with their pessimistic camp leader, scoutmaster lumpus, as they navigate camp life, rivalries with the all-female squirrel scouts from across the lake, and the unregulated wonders of nature.
pros: distinct joe murray visual aesthetics.
lumpus’s rage, pettiness and unhinged schemes provide the primary comedic value than cheap slapstick.
tom kenny’s voice acting performance.
slinkman’s deadpan bureaucratic delivery is a great grounding balance to lumpus’s manic narcissism.
creative parodies scout culture with absurd very damn specific badges and camp rituals.
cons: formulaic episode structure where lazlo’s harmless optimism disrupts camp rules, lumpus overreacts and lumpus ends up suffering the consequences.
lacks the sharp satirical edge, surreal darkness and hidden maturity.
lazlo is endlessly cheerful, imagine a monkey d. luffy without the growth or journey.
repetitive slapstick rarely serve unexpected outcomes.
background chars like edward, chip, skip and samson get buried to gag roles.
static environment where audience gets trapped in camp and flats gets tiring.
interactions with patsy smiles and the squirrel scouts repeats the same predictableness.
later seasons run thin on camp scenarios, mostly about recycled characters' stretched-out gags.
similarMedia: the grim adventures of billy & mandy

items.title: laughing stock
items.summaryPlot: an oblique concept album that follows a man's journey through a sinful life, suicide, ascension, and connection with god. it is a dark and spiritual journey exploring themes of death, redemption, and what comes after.
pros: production treats room ambience, mic bleed and prolonged silence as compositional instruments. using gaps as element is hard thing to do.
opening track is the record's restraint, using acoustic strums, distant vibraphone and quiet amp hum to create tension.
"ascension day" shifts from mark hollis’s murmurs into 9/8 drum patterns and guitar noise.
lee harris’s drum performance is extraordinary.
"after the flood" is 9-minute masterclass built around a hypnotic organ drone, weeping harmonica and slowly layering textures.
unconventional instrumentation & texture.
micro-details and layering with warmth.
"new grass" is transcendence with drum groove and guitar chords, is a meditative payoff with harmony.
cons: mumbled, indecipherable enunciation requires external factors to understand, crucial.
mid-section is about heavily dissonant horn swells and random guitar plucks that goes with formless ambient.
volume gap from whispers to explosive snares isn't really balanced or blended well.
instant track fade-outs feels unearned considering the rest of the songs.
closing track is so stark and minimalist and barely more than isolated guitar plucks, outros sometimes meant to be as this but it could've been way more creative than a gimmicky soft goodbye.
mediumInfluences: the black saint and the sinner lady

items.title: grace
items.summaryPlot: grace is a yearning meditation on time, death, and love. it is a deeply romantic and tragic record, featuring buckley repeatedly pining for an off-screen love interest while wrestling with his own mortality. the album channels diverse traditions—from jazz torch singers to heavy metal and pakistani qawwali—into an intense and profoundly moving experience.
pros: buckley’s vocal control is shifting from breathy, intimate falsettos to resonant belts is elite.
"hallelujah" is stripping leonard cohen’s synth-heavy original down to a solo fender telecaster and dynamic vocal delivery is timeless.
title track serve harmonic tension through shifting chord inversions before detonating into a ecstatic vocal crescendo.
"lover, you should've come over"  has earned emotional weight, by a melancholic harmonium pulse, weeping guitar arpeggios and deep lyricism.
complex harmonic chords & tuning.
opening track uses subtle guitar, vocal runs and unpredictable rhythmic shifts which builds an eerie soundscape.
orchestral performance is lush.
mick grøndahl (bass) and matt johnson (drums) serve fluid jazz inspired dynamics.
"dream brother" shows droning harmonium, percussive textures and modal guitar which feels haunting.
heavy distorted alt-rock riffing integration with overall lush energy.
shifting between delicate folk, classical hymns, led zeppelin-inspired heavy rock and soul.
cons: 3 out of the 10 tracks ("hallelujah", "lilac wine", "corpus christi carol") are covers. external factor that directly effects the experience but it's not too heavy of a con for me since it's mostly contextual which i don't care about.
buckley feels theatrical sometimes. extended vibrato and operatic flourishes feels annoying time to times.
underdeveloped lyricism on heavier tracks.
several tracks extend around 5-to-6-minute mark with repetitive grooves which should've been tightened.

items.title: wonderful rainbow
items.summaryPlot: the album is widely considered lightning bolt's most accessible work, featuring heavy, catchy bass riffs and frenetic drumming. it conjures a chaotic, abstract world described by critics as evoking "retarded unicorns" and "copulating robots," representing a cathartic journey through the interplay of chaos and order.
pros: chemistry between brian chippendale's polyrhythmic drumming and brian gibson's distorted bass is great, kinda gives a great wall of sound with just two instruments.
"dracula mountain" riff is hypnotic bass line that continuously carries up tension.
gibson strings his bass with banjo strings and cello tuning  with g-g-d-a,  feels crushing.
chippendale’s drum performance serve non-stop endurance, complex fills and erratic tempo with zero studio grid.
"2 morro morro land" bridges raw noise with bouncy videogame-like math-rock riffs.
vocal layers are alien-alike and blends in detached in a good way.
"dead cowboy" moves from an opening rhythm into a 8-minute noise crescendo.
intentional rubbish recording quality feels claustrophobic.
cons: album lacks breathing rooms and filled with nonstop full volume distortion. causes listening fatigue.
several tracks uses single riff for minutes without introducing any shift.
vocals are noise with zero lyrical or thematic content. while detached which is cool, seeks external factors to understand.
"30,000 monkeys" which is the closing track is abrasive finale without the tight architecture of other tracks.
entire record is made with one bass and one drum kit, variety is narrow and layers are poorly fed.
the most endings are generic fade-out effect.
distorted bass frequencies overwhelm the drum impact,
math rock element in album isn't tight and well-made compared to the genre standarts or essential works.

items.title: numb chucks
items.summaryPlot: two well-meaning but half-witted woodchuck brothers, dilweed and fungus, stumble upon a late-night infomercial for a kung-fu video featuring the legendary woodchuck morris. inspired by their new "mentor," they dedicate themselves to using their bungling martial-arts skills to protect the citizens of ding-a-ling springs—whether they need it or not.
pros: premise of two woodchucks attempting to use commercialized martial arts ("way of the chuck") to protect their town is easy to grasp.
11 minutes for this episodic show is safe scale.
satirization of cheesy 1980s martial arts video games is a consistent motif.
sound fx is rich and impactful in the show.
cons: dilweed and fungus are obnoxious brainless characters whose stupidity causes endless predictable and unearned misery for everyone around them.
humor leans on lazy graphic bodily fluids, boogers&barf or dumb butt jokes.
almost every single episode follows the same formula which is about the brothers misunderstand a daily situation, misuse a kung-fu technique, destroy the town and escape all consequences.
voice direction is about ear-jerking yelling that becomes exhausting within minutes.
standard character movement feels stiff, puppet-rigged and visually cheap.
zero emotionality or heart, show lacks any warmth, character relationships or heart, feels like hyperactive background noise.
side characters exist to scream or act mad.
predictable slapstick timing.
recycles the hyperactive idiot-duo of fanboy & chum chum or modern low-tier slapstick without adding any original layer.
similarMedia: cloudy with a chance of meatballs

items.title: sekiro shadows die twice
items.summaryPlot: in the late 1500s sengoku period, a shinobi known as wolf is defeated and left for dead while trying to rescue his young master, the divine heir kuro, from the clutches of the ashina clan's usurper, genichiro. revived with the power of resurrection, wolf must navigate a war-torn land, confront mythical creatures and fallen samurai, and sever the ties of immortality to free his master and reclaim his honor.
pros: sekiro's posture system, tools and combat layers are genius and consistent.
buddhist-inflected cycle of death/rebirth and link to mortality as meaning is executed effortlessly but impactful.
guardian ape's transition, the divine dragon's elegance and similar artistic choices enriches the overall theme of the product.
pattern recognition in combat is rewarding and strict, kinda feels like a smooth rhythm game.
lore is buried in item descriptions and passive storytelling, despite being a minimalistic and simple story, game forces active attention.
absence of collectibles and ubisoft alike open world interaction paradoxically enriches the organic exploration and rewarding.
replayability comes from the challenge itself, not from any extra content or elements.
kuro's journey, wolf's devotion and genichiro's nationalism is told by dialogues clues which respects the intelligence of the gamer.
sekiro forces mastery. gamer must adapt and learn to deflect quickly and combat system is just exceptional.
boss squad has zero fillers, minimal gimmick encounters and each boss comes up with unique patterns and rewarding combat system.
grappling hook and worldbuilding gives the gamer freedom to use environment to explore which also enriches the positioning in combat.
cons: building variety is way too limited compared to other soulslike games.
stealth mechanics in the game are optional but also incredibly primitive and shallow. quality stealth mechanic requires smart ai which doesn't exist in this game.
game's combat is incredible but it also contains over reliance on building posture and deflect mechanics which gets repetitive after a while.
consequences free instant resurrection devalues death.
my core problem with lore based video games is the fact that they seek external factors such as guides and wikis on understanding the story.
dragonrot mechanic is punishing without any rewards, turns the mechanic into a chore that must be managed.
several mini-boss archetypes such as headless, lone shadows, chained ogres are recycled multiple times.
key boss weaknesses are hidden in conversations which are obscure or easily missed.

items.title: half life 2
items.summaryPlot: gordon freeman awakens from stasis decades after the black mesa incident, finding earth conquered by the alien combine empire. now in the dystopian city 17, he joins a human resistance movement to fight back against the oppressive regime and its human administrator.
pros: physic engine is integration in combat successfully that makes the environmental combat engaging.
puzzles are solid, using the physic engine.
ravenholm chapter contains flawless action horror sequence where resource management, atmospheric horror elements and environmental combat with gravity gun is used.
oppression and world's ideology is shown through environmental storytelling and architecture.
level designs and pacing are so balanced and consistent that it overshadows most of the negatives by serving overall satisfying experience.

enemy and weapon variety are lacking and either shooting or puzzles aren't the peak in this game but it cannot be mattered when each chapter and level design serves unique content such as action horror, corridor shooting, physic puzzles, bugbait combat, overcharged gravity gun sequence, science fiction sequences, platformer beach sequence, narrow apartments, giant robots fights, cinematic sequences then street level sequences, wwii style beach warfare, vehicle driving sequences and mini open worlds with puzzles in it, this is insane amount of content paced balanced without artificially extended gameplay time.
tactical ai is actually solid, enemies constantly switch positions, track your positioning and throws grenades on covers.
character interactions and dialogues are designed organic and solid.
science fiction elements are fresh.
cons: route kanal and highway 17 damages runtime with floaty vehicle physics and repetitive open the gate interruptions.
gordon freeman’s silence doesn't add anything to game at all but looks awkward in emotional and action-packed dialogues.
guns such as smg are inconsistent, makes the enemies sandbag and isn't satisfying.
managing companion ai is annoying.
puzzles lacks quantity despite being quality, valve has made a whole brand with puzzles in it but that's external so it's a con in this game.

boss-fights consist of launching rockets randomly to the air so tracker can hit the helicopter which isn't near engaging, same for giant robots and probably any sequences that contains rocket launchers.
health, ammo and energy are given in bulks regularly in specific stations which kinda ruins the resource management element.

items.title: apostrophe
items.summaryPlot: the first side of apostrophe (') loosely follows a surreal, dreamlike narrative. it begins with the singer dreaming he is an eskimo named nanook, who gets into a confrontation about yellow snow, before transitioning to the bizarre "st. alfonzo's pancake breakfast". the rest of the album shifts to standalone tracks, including the mystical "cosmik debris," the socially conscious "uncle remus" on racism, and the humorous "stink-foot". the title track is a fusion instrumental featuring jack bruce on bass.
pros: features elite instrumental performances from george duke (keyboards), jean-luc ponty (violin), jack bruce (bass) and aynsley dunbar (drums).
apostrophe title track is heavy funk-rock instrumental duel between frank zappa's lead guitar and cream’s jack bruce on bass that ride the momentum.
album links four distinct movements such as "yellow snow", "nanook", "st. alfonzo", "father o'blivion" using intricate 5/4 and 7/8 time signature changes.
built around a filthy blues-guitar riff paired wit satire mocking fake spiritual gurus and mysticism.
recorded with hi-fi clarity, is crisp stereo separation, punching your face bass response and dynamic audio space.
classical-fusion runs that elevate "uncle remus" and the title track above standard rock elements.
uncle ramus track is co-written with george duke that serve social critique on civil rights dynamics over lush piano chords.
ruth underwood’s marimba and vibraphone add that distinct complexity to tight rhythm sections.
zappa’s guitar solos are raw and rejects generic blues cliches.
album's silly structure doesn't take itself serious and forces art music tropes while being art album.
cons: several impressive instrumental jams like the title track and "stink-foot" are fade-outs rather than definitive piece.
zappa's spoken word is usually too theatrical.
b side cannot keep the consistency in favor to lean more into comedic values.
gimmicky sound effects usage age worse than intrumental elements.
closing track is simple, plodding 4/4 funk beat over 6 minutes, trust a lot to vical gags.
album is a bit commercialized than what is a jazz fusion is.
excentrifugal forz feels unfinished.
similarMedia: we're only in it for the money

items.title: hounds of love
items.summaryPlot: hounds of love is structured as two distinct halves. the first side explores the ambiguities, fears, and vulnerabilities of romantic love. the second side, the ninth wave, is a seven-song conceptual suite following a woman drifting alone in the sea at night, tracing her journey through crisis, survival, and rebirth.
pros: running up that hill is built around an iconic linndrum rhythm and lush fairlight cmi synth textures.
kate bush just mastered cmi synthesizer which causes unique textures.
7-track b-side is high-concept about a person drifting at sea, struggling against drowning and sleep.
orchestral strings and military snares rides the momentum dynamically.
minimalist synth-stabs and claustrophobic vocal layering awakens paranoa and isolation.
irish instruments as fiddles, uilleann pipes and bodhrán joins with unexpected but fresh texture.
spoken-word samples, distorted vocal shifts and church-bell textures, that's rich catalog of elements used well in experimental scene.
bush' vocal control and range is unmatched.
album is divided into an accessible commercial a-side and experimental b-side.
storytelling is lyrically cinematic.
cons: reverb snare hits and early digital synths are dated and linked to commercial production tropes.
album sometimes is too theatrically melodramatic, it feels forced.
"the big sky" is monotonous wall-of-sound that doesn't evolve into something.
commercial studio polishing ruins the dreamy experimental approach.
some spoken word samples feels gimmicky.
commercial side of the album is about generic structure of repetitive and predictable verse-chorus boredom.
beat crafting and synth-loop repetitions lack glitch details and kinda falls as simple. well it was generational in it's time, i guess?

items.title: paranoid
items.summaryPlot: thematic exploration of the dark underbelly of the human experience and the anxieties of its era. it serves as a sonic journey through the societal ills of 1970, tackling the horrors of war ("war pigs"), mental health struggles ("paranoid"), drug addiction ("hand of doom"), and apocalyptic dread ("electric funeral"), while also showcasing the band's surprising versatility with a haunting, psychedelic interlude on "planet caravan."
pros: tony iommi’s tritone and pentatonic riffs in war pigs, iron man and electric funeral is fresh
war pig is very dynamic with heavy epicness with tempo shifts, guitar fills and a heavy climax.
bass lines leads melody and fills the awkward spaces successfully.
ward’s drumming is unpredictable, fills the melody and uses jazz dynamics that contain heavy riffs above simple 4/4 pounding.
lyrical themes deal with cold-war military, corruption, psychological decay, nuclear destruction and drug addiction using simple but impactful lyrics.
heavy riffs perfectly shades the mechanical plot of a time-traveling man turned to steel seeking vengeance.
psychedelic detour featuring flanged vocals, congas and jazz-guitar arpeggios with brilliant textures.
ozzy osbourne’s unpolished delivery screws through down tuned instrumentation with clean clarity.
rat salad solo is fun.
cons: title track was written as a quick 2-minute studio filler, relying on basic 3-chord punk/rock structures without any complexity.
rodger bain’s production lacks the raw bass wallop and crushing down-tuned heaviness.
multiple tracks rely on classic 100% studio fade-outs than musical resolutions.
early stereo mixing choices place the guitar hard-left and rhythm hard-right on certain sections which is distracting and aged poorly.
sonic and mechanical clarity is clearly not mastered due to release date.

planet caravan is a massive 4 minute pacing breaker between two accessible high melody tracks. it's not a bad track but could work as a intro. clearly off-genre and way too long for a bridge between two bangers.

items.title: terraria official soundtrack
items.summaryPlot: a dynamic, genre-blending instrumental soundtrack that serves as the audio identity for the 2d sandbox adventure game terraria, shifting from serene, ambient melodies for exploration to intense, high-energy orchestral anthems for epic boss battles. the music enhances the game's core themes of discovery, danger, and triumph, creating an immersive backdrop for the player's journey through a vast, procedurally generated world.
pros: soundtrack is iconic and instantly tone setting.
unique tracks for biomes as jungle, the hallow, corruption and desert give every region atmospheric signature.
boss tracks are chaotic and serves the same with rich synth and riff elements specifically track plantera which is influenced by the band pantera.
"underground" and "underworld" use basslines and sparse synth echoes to build isolation.
sudden event tracks as "goblin army," "pirate invasion" and "solar eclipse") shifts the exploration rhythm with synth pulses.
retro-modern blending is genius, album pulls the 8 bit/16 bit soundtrack structures and reshapes it with modern elementally rich touches.
melodies are catchy and memorable.
tracks like "frost moon" and "pumpkin moon" adapts to the theme of the event.
cons: if you stay in the same biome for an hour while grinding then soundtrack variety in the specific biome won't be too helpful.
waooohhh waaaaoohhhh waaaaoooohhh
soundtrack contains many goofy elements such as high-pitched chiptunes and laser-like synth.
early 1.0-era tracks uses dated synthesizers.
soundtrack is master at alienating audio but sitting through it causes listening fatique because synthetic structure.

items.title: berserk
items.summaryPlot: the story centers on guts, a lone swordsman branded for sacrifice, who is hunted by demonic forces in a brutal, medieval-inspired world. his quest for revenge against his former friend and leader, griffith, who betrayed their mercenary group in a horrific event known as the eclipse, is a harrowing exploration of fate, trauma, and the will to survive.
pros: kentaro miura’s artistic craftsmanship.
guts vs. griffith dynamic is engaging.
the golden age arc is a brilliant medieval military tragedy that earns every single emotional impact till eclipse.
combat is grounded and loyal to the worldbuilding's rules.
eclipse visuals betrayal, psychological weight and character dynamics in a peak way.
exploration of free will vs. causality is written solid.
transition from medieval military tactical wars to dark fantasy worldbuilding is brilliant.
guts’ painful transition from a suicidal and revenge-obsessed black swordsman back into a protective guardian contains insane character development.
every monstrous as zodd, wyald, mozgus and grunbeld are about unique human desires with disturbing presence.
cons: after tower of conviction, momentum slows down into a travelogue.
puck’s transformation into "chestnut puck" and isidro’s slapstick comedy breaks the atmosphere.
after kentaro miura's passing in 2021, the original creator's vision is never successfully mimicked.
the black swordsman and early lost children arcs are based on monster of the week trope.
early episodes had reliance on edgy shock value such as spamming of sexual violence, gore and childhood traumas, it is all earned but spammed a lot.
sea god feels like a rpg side-quest.
once falconia is appeared, griffith becomes a god and he doesn't need to be the smartest in the room to survive anymore.
casca being in a non-responsive mental state for over 200 chapters strips one of the story's strongest active characters.

items.title: the secret of kells
items.summaryPlot: in 9th-century ireland, young orphan brendan lives within the walled monastery of kells under the strict guardianship of his uncle, abbot cellach, who is obsessed with building walls to protect against viking raids. when the legendary illuminator brother aidan arrives with an unfinished manuscript, brendan defies his uncle to venture into the enchanted forest, where he meets the fairy aisling and confronts the serpent god crom cruach, all to complete the legendary book of kells.
pros: visual design mimics illuminated celtic manuscripts, strict symmetry and triptych framing, great for my perfectionist eyes.
debate between abbot cellach building a wall for survival and brother aidan crafting a book for cultural endurance serves grounded dilemma.
raider vikings are designed as monolithic figures which functioning as an force of nature if it makes sense.
brendan's descent into the pagan deity's cave shifts the animation into an abstract puzzle-fight that relies on geometry and survival.
film shows magic of art by showing the physical processes of medieval craftsmanship for example grinding gallnuts for ink, rendering emeralds and preparing parchment.
spoiler/ when the vikings finally come up, the film does not pull its punches, delivering a brutal massacre that breaks the reality of the threat.
separation between the oppressive linework of the abbot's tower and the organic linework of the forest builds has personality and identity.
background monks from italy, africa, etc. establish the abbey as an working knowledge without relying on lazy dumps.
cons: aisling’s fairy powers and the woodland magic is on unexplained logic which is soft magic that i dislike. i know it's folkrole but you can never feel any thrill or engagement in a story where magic could solve anything randomly.
brendan’s early interactions with aisling is about of forest exploration that stalls the narrative, pacing issue.
cellach's obsession with the wall becomes repetitive, acting as an plot roadblock.
brendan functions as a vessel for the plot.
chosen one tropes highly exists in looking through the eye of collumcille etc.
spoiler/ aisling’s final sacrifice or disappearance against the wolves happens abruptly.
until the wolf pack arrives, the forest is told as lighthearted that undermines the abbot's isolationist warnings, tonal disconnection here.
brendan and aidan’s escape from the viking massacre is about convenient timing and dense smoke which is not earned.

items.title: debut
items.summaryPlot: debut is a collection of diary-like fragments chronicling björk's arrival in london and her immersion in the early '90s club scene. the album serves as a sonic travelogue, exploring themes of alienation from an outsider's perspective with the wide-eyed wonder of an alien observing humanity. it navigates the chaotic joys of rave culture, the ecstasy of new love, and the search for identity after leaving behind the familiar sounds of her past.
pros: björk’s vocal performance is effortless from whispers to growls.
lush integration of bollywood-inspired strings recorded in mumbai on trip-hop groove is exotic.
successfully led the gap between underground alternative sensibilities and early-90s uk club/house music.
the track human behavior built around a looped sample of antônio carlos jobim’s "gaucho", it's just an swingy swingy rhythm section.
dropping electronic beats in to achive dissonant brass creates an organic atmospheric energy.
production collaboration joins the room with 90s dance-floor energy with punching the face basslines and synth layers.
tracks like "big time sensuality" and "crying" feature accessible vocal melodies with high replay value.
lyrics mimics childlike curiosity about human psychology and nature without forced stuff.
cons: production choices on tracks like "crying" and "violently happy" contain generic 4-on-the-floor house rhythms that have aged poorly.
compared to her rhuthm arrangements here are fairly basic and repetitive.
shift from explosive club tracks to sparse jazz feels disjointed.
underdeveloped avant-garde fits into standard pop verse-chorus formats.
repetitive vocals on "violently happy" goes with vocal stutters and repeated phrases in whole 5 minutes.
album feels like a collection of distinct pop experiments rather than a conceptual album experience.
complex woodwind/brass elements clash slightly with the swing elements.

items.title: terraria
items.summaryPlot: long ago, the ancient race of dryads went to war with the cosmic entity cthulhu, tearing off some of his limbs before he retreated to the dark side of the moon. centuries later, you, the terrarian, venture into the world to stop cthulhu—now known as the moon lord—for good.
pros: unlike traditional sandbox routine where gamer imagination decided the content, terraria marks clear objectives such as bosses as gates.
melee, ranged, summoner and magic classes has insane item and customization variety.
world layering with surface, underground and hell creates sense of danger and worldbuilding.
mid game unlocks hardmode which changes the whole structure of the worldbuilding with new challenging enemies and brand new biomes, ores and items.
invasions, blood moons and solar eclipses breaks the game loop and tests gamer's build and base safety with challenging enemy waves.
movement pacing is insane, from barely jumping to double jump, grappling hooks and wings system is rich and satisfying.
unique biome mechanics such as jungle poison hazards, desert sandstorms and underworld lava force players to adapt their gear and strategies per region.
boss fights are mostly solid, there are some fillers but the most main bosses requires strict patterns, skills and combat building variety.

sandbox elements favors co-op engagement, designing your own competitive ball sport with your own arena and rules, dealing with complex electric mechanism and activities such as golf, tower defense minigames are fun to engage with.
cons: progression in game strictly requires external factors as wikis and guide. i show no tolerance on reliance to external factors.
some crucial items has obscure rng drop rates which makes it farming chore to gain them.
expansion of corruption/crimson and hollow is annoying, they harass your custom world and only way to stop them is buying too expensive gears, which is also a boring waste of time to use them.
npc requirements are shallow. you put a table, chair and source of light and town-management is over. npc happiness and trading elements are way too surface level.
arena construction is repetitive and time wasting. placing all of the buff items and preparing a boss arena all yourself is annoying.
classes like summoner has awkward progression compared to more straightforward builds.

game's core pacing is totally broken. grinding for hours, mining and fishing for specific items, finding keys and dealing with low drop rates just to fight a boss is frustrating chore of dozens of hours.
strongest weapons in the game are gifted after defeating the final boss so gamer has no place to use them except for pointless power fantasy by defeating the previous bosses.

items.title: moby dick
items.summaryPlot: the wandering sailor ishmael signs onto the whaling ship pequod, unaware that its captain, ahab, is driven by a monomaniacal quest for revenge against the massive white sperm whale that bit off his leg on a previous voyage. as the pequod sails across the world's oceans, ahab's obsession consumes the crew and ship, leading them on a fateful chase that culminates in a catastrophic final confrontation with the whale.
pros: captain ahab’s obsessive vengeance against moby dick is focused.
white whale is actually symbolism for fate.
pequod’s multi-race crew is a fascinating society with class dynamics..
new bedford and nantucket establishing ishmael’s worldview and bond with queequeg is exceptional beginning.
descriptions of lowering boats and harpooning in open waters is actually realistic and tactical.
ahab vs. starbuck ideological clash is written well.
pequod’s crossing through other ships like jeroboam, samuel enderby and rachel points alternate faith.
ahab’s internal monologues are successfully shakespearean.
the chase of moby dick is a chaotic earned payoff.
cons: dozens of chapters are textbook essays on whale anatomy, history and classification which doesn't trust the reader slightly. also why teach whale anatomy when it's a symbolism?
ishmael starts as active in the story but vanishes as a character in the second half.
switches between adventure and shakespearean script layouts then scientific treatises is tonal betrayal and inconsistency.
middle part stretches voyage drift by ignoring plot progression.
determinism often limits suspension and forces tryhardness.
early figures like queequeg are gone into the background once the ship sets sail.
biblical allegory feels essayistic than organic.
ishmael's miraculous survival in floating on queequeg's coffin is unearned. i'm aware it's a metaphor on rebirth or something, it's not about realism i don't even see it as any quality metaphor.
mediumInfluences: the tragedy of the whaleship essex

items.title: ergo proxy
items.summaryPlot: set in a post-apocalyptic future within the domed utopia of romdo, inspector re-l mayer investigates a series of murders committed by autoreiv androids infected with the "cogito virus" that grants them self-awareness. the investigation pulls her into a global conspiracy involving vincent law, an immigrant haunted by his past, and mysterious god-like beings called "proxies," forcing them all to confront the true nature of their existence.
pros: romdeau city serves rich dystopian city atmosphere and dynamics with hierarchy and propaganda.
androids (autoreivs) acquiring self-awareness and emotional souls via a virus is a strong concept.
sharp usage of dark coloured shadows, rain and lighting gives early episodes a neo-noir tone.
the mystery of proxy project serves engaging mystery.
pino which is a autoreiv dressed in a rabbit suit is surprisingly a good companion.
references to descartes, rené magritte and mythologies can be found in the worldbuilding.
fights are grounded and realistic physically.
psychological decay is served as a deep element across characters.
cons: middle act contains episodic fillers.
mechanics such as the pulse of the awakening, amrita cells, the creators' return plan etc etc are served as complex infodumps.
animation quality is visibly inconsistent in later acts.
final of the show is rushed with overcrowded reveals.
jumping from massacres to surreal comedy-quiz episodes is tonal inconsistency.
journey across the ruined wasteland visits fails with domes that feel placeholders than real societies.
many episodes works with hallucinatory or subconscious dreamlike visuals, it creates forced obscurity in such physical story.
some of the bigger picture concepts such as fate of the returning true humans from orbit slowly decays, decays and gets forgotten.
similarMedia: ghost in the shell stand alone complex
mediumInfluences: nausicaä of the valley of the wind

items.title: cryostasis sleep of reason
items.summaryPlot: in 1981, russian meteorologist alexander nesterov is sent to investigate the nuclear icebreaker north wind, which has been trapped in arctic ice since 1968. upon arrival, he discovers the crew has been mutated into bizarre creatures, and he must use his unique ability, the "mental echo"—which allows him to enter the memories of the dead and change their past actions—to uncover the ship's tragic mystery. as he navigates the frozen vessel, he finds fragments of maxim gorky's fairy tale that parallel the ship's fate, forcing him to confront the nature of tragedy and whether the past can ever truly be rewritten.
pros: possessing the memories of dead crewmen to alter their past actions (closing a pressure valve, throwing a switch) to fix environmental elements in the present is a top-tier puzzle mechanic.
body-heat managing system replaces traditional health with body temperature.
frost accumulate on your weapon and vision in real time when entering unheated zones.
serves a claustrophobic and isolated survival horror setting.
melee combat (water pipes, axes) and primitive soviet firearms (mosin-nagant, ppsh-41) has heavy momentum and swing animations.
gorky’s fairy tale of danko's burning heart is a commentary on leadership, sacrifice and the captain's decisions.
enemies are mutated crewmen bound to their cold-weather gear and industrial tools (welders, chain-men, projectionists), they're very spooky and atmospheric.
dynamic melting physics in real-time is satisfying.
zero hud system and heat bar adds up to atmosphere visually.
cons: atmosfear engine damaged by frame drops, memory leaks and performance hitches, even on high-end modern hardware.
level layouts are repetitive corridors which gets boring quickly.
protagonist moves at an slow walking pace, making backtracking or dodging enemy attacks feel like torture..
certain flashback sequences ask for untelegraphed steps that result in instant failure if not executed perfectly so be ready for absolute ragebait.
enemy ai is inconsistent and glitchy. enemies constantly stuck on doors and walls or they act dumb.
late game enemies are ammo-sponge. game wants you to use a shot and step back strategy which is dull, lazy and tired.
final boss fight inconsistencies in the final confrontation, from the established fps survival gameplay, mechanics-wise feeling out of place.
despite the giant ship, levels are linear with minimal room for walking around or exploratory sequences are dull..
key triggers like tiny light switches or hidden ladder rungs are poorly displayed in dark rooms, causes aimless moments.
similarMedia: call of cthulhu dark corners of the earth

items.title: omori
items.summaryPlot: the player controls sunny, a mute hikikomori teenage boy, and his dream world alter-ego omori. while omori explores the vibrant yet surreal dream world of headspace with his friends, sunny navigates the real world of faraway town, and the player's choices determine whether sunny confronts or continues to suppress the traumatic truth behind his sister mari's death.
pros: tying emotional states (happy > angry > sad > happy) serves a clever tactical layer to turn-based battles.
tonal dynamic of pastel headspace dream world and the claustrophobic real world faraway town builds strong psychological anchor.
plot is haunting, dealing with repression, memory suppression and the psychological weight of a secret delivers gravity.
black space horror sequences has exceptional horror atmosphere and environmental storytelling.
party members accumulating energy to perform followed attacks is great at team positioning and combos.
decisions unlocks different content and ending.
hand drawn art is memorable and unique.

side quests consist of odd jobs around faraway town such as delivering pizzas, raking leaves, helping neighbors, this is surprisingly grounded and actually serves to theme when narrative needs that contrast to soften the heaviness of dream dungeons, they feel human.

sunny's phobias such as heights, water and spiders actually blended cleverly to the gameplay, which makes psychological weight earned. this is shocking to me, games probably leaves it as context or organic excuse to the technological limitations.
cons: sweetheart's castle or the humphrey whale contains a lot of cheap fetch quests.
outside of major boss fights, turn-based enemy encounters is mindless button-mashing routines which lacks any depth or engagement.

silly cartoon antics in headspace interrupt darkness and psychological tension built in real world. it could be seen as escapism cope but doesn't change the fact that it damages the tonal consistency and could've done better. audience doesn't need obvious tropes to see coping idea which is obvious, that's disrespectful.
searching for hidden computer keys is artificial completionist chore.
real-world encounters are about basic attack and item commands.
spoiler/ for psychological thriller readers as me, the twist on mari's death contains many predictable cliché psychological tropes.
late-game bosses force tedious grinding in headspace to boost hp and juice pools which is chore and repetitive grind which i hate.
heavy backtracking and navigation in bigass areas like the junkyard or deep well is just walking repetitively in empty vastness.
dream-world companions are generic and repetitive "friendship power-of-love" trope which is i guess crucial in standard jrpgs.
ending is rushed and game leaves the gamer with many questions, fast executions and lazy shortcuts.

items.title: stalker
items.summaryPlot: in an unspecified soviet-era wasteland, a guide known as the stalker leads a writer and a professor through a forbidden, surreal area called the zone, where a mysterious room is said to grant a visitor's innermost desires. the journey becomes an existential pilgrimage, forcing each man to confront the nature of his own faith, cynicism, and deepest hidden self.
pros: switching from piss filter to vibrant colours in the industrial town has great visual function and symbolization.
decaying and abandoned industrial ruins of the zone creates atmosphere of post-apocalyptic decay.
a place that grants a person's subconscious desire than a grant wish is a brilliant psychological element..
using nut-throwing to detect unseen gravitational anomalies is great invisible danger.
tragicomic possibility of "what if zone doesn't even working, is the zone even real?" questions actually create a great what-if irony.
spoiler/ realization that the men are terrified to enter the room because they fear their own subconscious is powerful philosophy and the final bomb twist is well-made.
cinematography & camera movement supports the dreamy like atmosphere.
spoiler/ they don't enter the room at the end!
cons: physical nature of the zone's traps is abstract, i know it meant to be abstract but the whole movie feels like actionless indiana jones movie with all that reaching a macguffin (the room) after passing through traps and claustrophobic sequences in who-knows-what-it-is place. mystery can be explained in a way that it wouldn't feel shallow. this way, everything is an excuse.

worldbuilding, magical zone and room structure, human factors and characters itself, even plot are just excuse to throw three different guys on forced philosophical dialogues without organic structure throughout the movie than showing the philosophy.

because no traps are visually shown triggering on screen, the danger claimed by the stalker character feel artificial. it could be seen as some mental gymnastics defense as "but traps are internal and it reflects something something about stalker." yeah i could defend literally anything with that attitude by manipulating philosophy and logic.

movie is too abstract that if you start talking about what you philosophically see in the movie straightforwardly then you'll inevitably sound forced and delusional and that's the movie on the blame. sometimes movie feels like "winnie the pooh is peak fiction because all characters reflect different psychological issues." like shut the fuck up. non-clarity is being spectrum, being spectrum is playing safe, playing safe is hollow.

items.title: arcana heart 3
items.summaryPlot: two months after the "great kanto incident" of arcana heart 2, dimensional rifts begin appearing across japan, and rumors circulate that the drexler institute—a defunct organization that once distributed demonic arts throughout europe—has resumed operations. the japanese spirit agency dispatches their sacred maidens to investigate, while the newly established rosenberg branch office also deploys their own forces, setting the stage for a confrontation between the maidens and a new foe known as valkyries.
pros: d-button homing mechanic lets multi-directional dashes, tracking cancels and momentum shifts.
decoupling characters from their elemental spirits which named arcanas lets any fighter to equip any arcana, this means hundreds of different tactical variations.
extend force causes temporary access to unique arcana attributes, speed boosts and powerful arcana eclipse at the cost of meter management.
screen space and triple-jump/homing mechanics serves great fightings which rarely seen in traditional ground-based fighters.
hitboxes trigger a clash state rather than trade damage, this means better attack timing and cancel reactions.
despite the aesthetics, characters has variety with mechanical types, from puppet characters (lieselotte) to grapplers (kira) to set-play traps (scharlachrot).
cancels and inputs are fluently responsive.
complex homing-cancel combos are strict with high barrier .
cons: reliance on heavy fan-service.
story is generic visual-novel dialogue about saving japan from dimensional collapse cliche.
some arcana/character combinations with same loops and unreactable mix-ups dominates the play.

stacking homing trails, arcana visual effects, meter bursts and large side bar, character hurtboxes and projectiles gives headache when gamer has to focus and side-panel hud is an animated chibi reaction portraits with unnecessary distracting noise.
because the homing system is universal, many defensive scramble situations turns into predictable routines.
audios aren't rich, the same annoying anime screams and generic rock music bumps your head throughout the game.
ragnarok is an arcade boss which is a giant screen-filling gimmicky hotbox.
similarMedia: under night in birth exe late

items.title: adventure time
items.summaryPlot: set in the post-apocalyptic land of ooo a thousand years after a catastrophic nuclear war known as the "mushroom war," the series follows the adventures of finn the human, a young heroic boy, and his best friend and adoptive brother jake, a dog with the magical ability to change size and shape at will. together, they explore the strange and magical world of ooo, rescuing princesses, battling monsters, and helping the eccentric inhabitants of the land while gradually uncovering the mysteries of the past.
pros: post apocalyptic lore is very rich and constantly told by background environmental details.
finn actually gets more mature and evolves by time.
simon petrikov’s transition, marceline's backstory and tragedy elements are written solid.
world building and class division is well crafted, the land of ooo features candy kingdom, ice kingdom, fire kingdom with socio-political dynamics.
show contains experimental episodes such as "a glitch is a glitch" and "food chain" which pushed boundaries beyond standard animation.
princess bubblegum's authoritian personality questions the morality in leadership passively.
evolving dynamic between marceline and princess bubblegum serves a mature decades-spanning dynamic.
finn and jack aren't important to the lore, they're just living thousands of years later important historical events.
even though show is slapstick and light, audience feels that heaviness of the universe passively.
despite being lightweight, 10 minutes of early episodes serves much entertain value.
cons: show is 10 seasons and the most of this screentime is made of fillers, aimless episodes or backstories.
humor relies on cheap "lol how random" humor most of the time.
fantasy rules such as power dynamics, elemental logic and magic systems are just there without any explanation or direct origin (mostly).

major ongoing plot points such as finn's dad, vampires, marceline's father, the lich or golb are just there and scattered through multi seasons which causes pacing fatique than mystery and these are solved mostly cheaply and again with "lol so that's it? alright" humor.
dozens of creatures and gigantic mythologies only exist for specific episodes then never to be seen again.

lore is mostly told by backstories unrelated to finn and jack which ruins the whole build up for "world's scars based" storytelling. what's the point of designing main characters which are unimportant to the world if audience won't figure out the lore from current scars of the environmental storytelling parallelly with them? but nah they decided to show the direct story visually unrelated to them, it's okay that lore isn't related to them that's the point but storytelling mustn't.
finn's early romantic interests are instantly dropped after a while, that's one of the weakest aspects of finn's personal evolution.

middle seasons are suffered by pacing issues because show suddenly decided to drop episodic structure and become philosophical media. weird decision by a show that wanted to be episodic lightweight humor with never explained fillers structure.

show decides to introduce finn and jack with a grounded non heroic but just living their life structure then decided to crown them for being heroes of the universe anyways. a show that never meant to be epic betrays its own concept by being epic.
similarMedia: kipo and the age of wonderbeasts

items.title: stardew valley
items.summaryPlot: after inheriting your deceased grandfather's dilapidated farm in the rural town of stardew valley, you leave the soulless corporate grind behind to start a new life. you must restore the farm to its former glory, build relationships with the townspeople, and choose whether to revitalize the town's crumbling community center or side with the soulless joja corporation, all while uncovering the secrets of the valley.
pros: whole game is a clear checklist simulator.
ticking clock and stamina bar force daily planning, route planning and task prioritization.
unlocking sprinklers, auto-feeders and junimo huts systematically removes manual labor and rewards planning.
fishing minigame requires timing and reaction skill rather than passive button-mashing.
seasons and weather comes up with unique events and festivals.
variety is insane, content is still ongoing after 100+ hours of gameplay.
npcs has light but effective backstories, town contains gossip lore and mystery, solving the mysteries and worldbuilding by playing is rewarding.
game requires zero wiki or guide, some aspects are harsh to find but game rewards patience and attention over wiki.
most systems are interconnected unlike most life and farming rpgs.
town and interior customization is solid.
game has dozens of micro management elements which mimicks the urgency of real life, this is a positive as a life sim.
cons: you can never go bankrupt or lose your farm; even passing out simply results in a minor energy or fee penalty, game is way too cozy despite having deep content. i'm not blaming coziness, i blame the game design by picking the route when had potential. so again "game is cozy" could be used to counter any criticism against the game so i don't accept it.
dungeon crawler combat is primitive. low weapon variety, zero strategy and positioning but just button-smashing. considering the total time you'd spend in mines, enemies becomes chore than threat.

before all of the automation systems that requires hours of manual work to achieve, gameplay is about doing dozens of activities and farm chores every 14 minutes. this is a crucial con that turns the game into a repetitive daily tasks loop.

most daily repetitive chores doesn't even reward or punish. if you won't feed your animals, log your kegs, kiss your partner, take care of your greenhouse, pet your cat, you won't be punished sligthly, which makes the gamer question why'd they even bother?
npc friendship is about formulaic spam of gifting them their fav things twice a week, which ignores any human relationship, psychological depth and logical rpg depth.

crop and artisan prices are fixed, economy never shapeshifts or market's global needs never changed, which doesn't stop a gamer from doing the same chore to become millionaire, so if you switch chores then that's just decisive.
single daytime is extremely short and daily routines drains the majority of the day which leaves no space to explore, grind or socialize.
rpg part of the game is shallow, when a dialogue appears, there is an obvious answer and a ragebait. also interaction with npcs is very limited.
certain community center bundles and museum donations rely on rng drops which is not related to skill or strategy.

absence of any risk management makes all of the micro calculations and prioritization meaningless. gamers think of "if i miss this, i'll have to wait another year" than "if i miss this, i'll face the consequences."
similarMedia: story of seasons friends of mineral town

items.title: oliver twist
items.summaryPlot: oliver twist, an orphan born in a workhouse, endures a miserable childhood of child labor before escaping to london, where he falls in with a gang of pickpockets led by the elderly criminal fagin. after being wrongly accused of theft, oliver is rescued by the kind mr. brownlow, but the gang recaptures him, leading to a series of events that ultimately reveal oliver's true identity and secure his happy ending.
pros: satire execution is sharp, book clearly shows hypocrisy of victorian poor law.
london's labyrinthine and claustrophobic environment is atmospheric.
book contains many memorable figures such as fagin, the artful dodger and bill sikes.
chertsey burglary planning is actually serving tension and execution is tight.
psychological depth isn't any surface level, for example nancy’s murder captures guilt, paranoia and psychological collapse.
book rejects victorian romanticism by directly showing child exploitation, urban poverty and systemic corruption.
settings dynamics as shift from claustrophobic london streets to safe countryside is effective.
artful dodger’s courtroom scene is damn good, provides street-smart coolness and uses quality satire elements.
morale stakes are clear, for example reader is left with tension of "will twist stay still pure after all of these?"
cons: oliver usually survive through pure luck, external factors and helpless innocence.
book excuses heavy coincidences like oliver's burglary spot is being his wealthy relatives.
oliver is unrealistically untainted by his surroundings despite growing up in a workhouse, kinda points cheap melodrama effect.
resolution relies on lazy secret plotline.
figures like mr. brownlow and rose maylie are unrealistically purely good despite living in a corrupted state.
subplots are conversational fillers that slows down the book's pacing.
dickens frequently pauses the story just to lecture the reader on victorian morality and christian charity like we are dumbass.
some key figures like monks are just cheap plot summaries.
tonal shift is inconsistent by shifting victorian romance and crime thriller awkwardly.

items.title: resident evil
items.summaryPlot: in 1998, members of the elite police task force s.t.a.r.s. are sent to investigate a series of gruesome murders in the arklay mountains, only to be attacked by monstrous dogs and forced to take refuge in a mysterious, zombie-infested mansion. as chris redfield or jill valentine, players must explore the mansion, solve puzzles, and uncover the nightmarish truth behind the umbrella corporation's secret biological experiments in order to survive and escape.
pros: architecture of the mansion is interconnected and atmospheric.
limited resources management creates tension by forcing gamers to choose between fighting or strategically escaping from enemies.
fixed camera is claustrophobic and serves to theme.
sound design with elements such as creaking floorboards, door opening audio and uncanny music builds environmental pressure.
enemy introductions such as zombies and dogs are very iconic, spooky and impactful.
puzzles are usually environmental and actually rewarding.
late game introduces way faster and lethal enemies which forces gamer to adapt or surrender.
cons: 6 to 8 inventory grid is too strict even for resource management element where you get a weapon, two magazines and a story item, and now you don't have a space for a key for a crucial door. also this issues leads to backtrackings constantly.

game wants you to play the game twice and only thing it serves for it is having two characters with minimal differences. the only differences between first and second gameplay is basically just some extra minor cutscenes which doesn't worth it.
voice acting in gaming wasn't a real industry back then so voice acting sucks.
requiring a limited consumable item just to save progress leads to loss of progress from unearned cheap deaths.
game has dozens of b movie elements which looks cheesy and aged awful.
primitive tank controls are simply annoying, even aiming, which is crucial, is pain.
the most doors has a five seconds opening animations, some of these contain impactful jumpscares but interrupting the game everytime opening a door is poor designing.
combat is stiff and basic with auto-aim and obscure skill gaps.
chris redfield starts with less inventory grids and no lockpick, this is just artificial difficulty.
final laboratory sequences are uninspired in design compared to early gothic mansion.
crucial puzzle items are very easy to miss without external factors such as guides and wikis, i personally show zero tolerance to reliance on external factors.

items.title: nineteen eighty four
items.summaryPlot: in a grim, totalitarian superstate called oceania, where the omniscient "big brother" and the thought police monitor every action and thought, a disillusioned outer-party member named winston smith works at the ministry of truth rewriting historical records to match the party's ever-changing narrative. yearning for freedom, winston begins a forbidden love affair with julia and joins a secret revolutionary group called "the brotherhood," but their rebellion is doomed, leading to his capture, torture in the infamous room 101, and eventual complete betrayal of his own mind.
pros: mechanics of oceania such as big brother, tele-screens, the four ministries really create a terrifying total-control..
newspeak designed to limit the range of human thought by destroying vocabulary is a masterclass concept.
psychology requiring citizens to hold two beliefs and accept both as true offers fascinating depth.
oppressive atmosphere successfully creates claustrophobia.
o'brien's dialogue in the ministry of love rejects basic villain tropes.
junior spies program turning children into state informants against their own parents creates domestic distrust.
memory hole and rewriting of historical newspaper archives creates the control feeling over truth.
room 101 phobia exploitation directly terrorize human loyalty and identity.
without spoilers, conclusion is quality written, rejecting hero tropes.
cons: goldstein's book damages the pacing by placing manifestos in an ongoing story.

large portion of the book is just socio-political ideas disguised as a narrative. book reads as a guy with massive vision but very messy creative urge and had to write something just to push his ideas.

as you can see, majority of the pros are about critical worldbuilding rather than narration. this book is overally a socio-political text rather than narration. i don't need this narration to learn about these ideas in atmospheric passive story. i already know totalitarianism is bad, i need a narrative that makes me feel that, this clearly can't. probably did and popularized it decades ago but i'd be careless.

proles are passive mass that never evolves beyond background. they're too broken then what's the difference between them and random ass brainwashed individual? probably that states actually cannot control them right? well so zero impact on the story than flexing the atmosphere of oppression even more like it's not already enough.
relationship between winston and julia is a rebellion against party rules than chemistry which is lack of human element, it adds sub romance element as a filler.

wars between oceania, eurasia and eastasia are ambiguous, which doesn't inform the reader slightly about political aspect of the globe. i guess book thinks it doesn't even matter since wars are just excuse yet i'll tak it as a plot hole here because even central focus is atmosphere, wars are atmosphere, anything is.
early chapters are about winston's daily misery and diary writing paranoia multiple times before any plot progression.

characters like parsons exist just to throw out some caricaturistic unearned brainwashed loyalty figures which is arguably also brainwashing. writing whole new character just to show how brainwashed people are, is not necessary because it's a basic observation.
heavy determinism limits the story engagement in the middle parts.

items.title: bully
